title: Blue Tokai crosses Rs 500 Cr revenue in FY26; losses up 54%
summary:
Coffee chain Blue Tokai continued to expand its business in FY26, with revenue crossing the Rs 500 crore mark, supported by its presence in the organised cafe market. However, the expansion came with a higher cost burden, as losses widened 53.7% during the fiscal year ended March 2026.
Blue Tokai’s revenue from operations surged 59.4% to Rs 518 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 325 crore in FY25, according to the company’s consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.


The company also reported Rs 7.5 crore in other income, pushing its total income to Rs 525.5 crore during the last fiscal year.

Sales of coffee and related products remained Blue Tokai’s primary source of operating revenue, rising 59.3% to Rs 513 crore in FY26 from Rs 322 crore in FY25. Lease income increased 36.2% to Rs 3.5 crore, while revenue from services stood at Rs 1 crore during the fiscal year.
The increase in operating costs outpaced revenue growth, putting pressure on Blue Tokai’s profitability. The cost of materials consumed, its largest cost component, increased 65.5% to Rs 187 crore in FY26 from Rs 113 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses rose 35.9% to Rs 130.5 crore, while rent expenses grew 59.6% to Rs 26.65 crore during the last fiscal year.
Depreciation costs nearly 2X jumped to Rs 87 crore. Finance costs also jumped 68.8% to Rs 27 crore from Rs 16 crore in the same period.
Other expenses grew 70.5% to Rs 150 crore in FY26 from Rs 88 crore in FY25, accounting for 25% of the total expenditure. Consequently, the Gurugram-based company's total expenses increased 61.7% to Rs 608 crore in FY26 from Rs 376 crore in the previous fiscal year.
On the profitability front, Blue Tokai's EBITDA stood at Rs 23 crore in FY26, compared with Rs 19.4 crore in FY25. However, its EBITDA margin declined to 4.44% from 5.97%. The company's net losses widened 53.7% to Rs 83 crore in FY26 from Rs 54 crore in the previous fiscal year.


Blue Tokai's return on capital employed (ROCE) stood -11.94% in FY26. On a unit level, the firm spent Rs 1.17 to  earn a rupee in the same period.

The company's cash and bank balances declined to Rs 39 crore in the last fiscal year from Rs 118 crore in FY25. Meanwhile, its total assets increased to Rs 697 crore from Rs 521 crore previous fiscal year.
Blue Tokai operates in an increasingly competitive coffee market, with Third Wave Coffee among its main rivals. Third Wave is yet to disclose its FY26 financial results, while Tata Starbucks reported operating revenue of Rs 1,367 crore and a 27% reduction in net losses during the year. 
The comparison highlights the gap in scale as Blue Tokai seeks to strengthen its position in India’s organised cafe market. Its next phase will depend on growing its store network while improving store-level economics, customer retention and op-efficiency. Building scale without adding proportionate costs will remain central to its path to profitability.

title: ShareChat parent crosses Rs 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26, posts Rs 672 Cr loss
summary:
It has been around 11 years since ShareChat started building its business around India's vernacular internet audience. The company has often been projected as a potential rival to Meta in India, but it is yet to give any meaningful competition to the social media giant. While ShareChat continues to experiment with new formats and has recently entered the microdrama segment to keep up with the trend, the business is still struggling to move towards profitability.
We are decoding its annual results for FY26. After two years of moderate growth in FY24 and FY25, ShareChat's revenue from operations grew 40.5% to Rs 1,016 crore in FY26 from Rs 723 crore in FY25.
Its parent company, Mohalla Tech, operates a vernacular social media and digital entertainment business through platforms such as ShareChat, Moj and QuickTV, targeting regional-language audiences in India.
Revenue from ShareChat's chatroom feature, where users can interact through video calls, accounted for 46% of its total operating revenue. This segment grew 8.8% to Rs 471 crore in FY26. Meanwhile, advertising revenue declined 13% to Rs 252 crore during the year.
On the other hand, QuickTV contributed Rs 293 crore in subscription revenue in FY26. Unlike advertising revenue, subscription revenue is recognised over the subscription period. The company also added Rs 89 crore through the reversal of provisions for doubtful assets, taking its total income to Rs 1,105 crore.

As the company continues to push its new business verticals, its business development expenses surged 8.7X to Rs 335 crore in FY26 from Rs 43 crore in FY25. Following layoffs over the past year, employee benefit expenses declined 16% to Rs 220 crore. We have excluded ESOP expenses of Rs 739 crore and Rs 184 crore in FY26 and FY25, respectively, from this comparison, as these are non-cash expenses.
The company also spent Rs 549 crore on interest expenses against its borrowings through debt securities. Server costs, content development, legal and other overheads pushed its overall expenses up 14.6% to Rs 1,777 crore in FY26 from Rs 1,550 crore in FY25.
While QuickTV has added a new revenue stream to the business, it is yet to translate into meaningful improvement in profitability. Mohalla Tech's net loss, however, narrowed 15.58% to Rs 672 crore in FY26 from Rs 796 crore in FY25.
We have not excluded ESOP expenses and unrealised foreign exchange losses while calculating the overall losses to give a fair picture of the company's financial performance. On a unit level, Mohalla Tech spent Rs 1.75 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, while its EBITDA margin stood at -84%.
Yes, ShareChat and Moj together have a user base of over 300 million, and with such a large audience, QuickTV could turn out to be a big opportunity for the company if it gets things right. However, the decline in advertising revenue also raises questions about whether brands are finding the right audience on its platforms or shifting their preference elsewhere. Even the chatroom segment, which contributes the largest share of revenue, is growing at a moderate pace. The next couple of years will be quite important for Mohalla Tech as it tries to build new revenue streams, make better use of its existing user base and, more importantly, move towards profitability.

title: Festive boost: D2C startups bag every third funding deal in October
summary:
Indian startup funding witnessed a sharp slowdown in October, but consumer-focused brands showed resilience. D2C startups raised around $200 million during the month, which was nearly 30% of the total $678 million raised by Indian startups.
In terms of deal volume, D2C startups accounted for 36 of the 108 deals recorded in October, which was 33.33% of the total. Their share was higher than the 20.36% recorded in H1 2026, when they secured 125 of the 614 deals, and 21.57% in Q3 2026, with 55 deals out of 255. This points to a growing share of consumer focused brands in India's startup funding activity.
In terms of deal value, D2C startups raised a little over $1 billion during the first nine months of 2026, which accounted for around 10% of the more than $10 billion raised by Indian startups during the period.
The strong showing by consumer brands comes at an important time as companies prepare for the festive and wedding seasons, when consumer spending typically picks up. For these startups, fresh capital could help them build inventory, expand distribution, strengthen supply chains and increase marketing spend to capture a larger share of the market.
According to Entrackr's funding data, consumer focused startups attracted investments across categories such as fashion, beauty, food, wellness, lifestyle and home products.


Food and beverages emerged as the largest category with eight deals, followed by fashion and lifestyle and health and wellness, which attracted seven deals each. Home and living brands secured six deals, while beauty and personal care companies accounted for four deals. Together, these five categories represented 32 of the 36 D2C funding deals recorded during the month, accounting for nearly 89% of the total.
Sports and fitness brand Boldfit topped the list with a $42 million Series B round led by Bharat Value Fund. Design led lifestyle brand DailyObjects followed with a $35 million Series C round, backed by Xponentia Capital Partners, Anicut Capital and Asia Private Capital.
Beauty and wellness brand Nat Habit raised $15 million in a Series C round led by Trident Growth Partners, while men's bottomwear brand The Pant Project secured $11.5 million in a Series B round led by Mirae Asset Venture Investment.
Food and consumer brands also attracted investor interest. Troovy raised $10.5 million in a Series B round led by Sharrp Ventures. Beyond Appliances, a smart kitchen technology company, also secured $11.5 million from Fireside Ventures.
Several other consumer brands raised capital during the month. These included Ace Blend ($9.91 million), MakeO ($9.5 million), Rotoris ($7.4 million), ChapterHome ($6.4 million), Kisah ($3.7 million), SuperMush ($3 million), The Stack ($2.2 million), Gramiyaa ($2 million). Smaller rounds also came from brands such as Lorazzo, Bangalore Watch Company, ReplyAll, So/Facet, Zinara, ISLAND Beauty and Qiroko.
The timing of these investments is particularly relevant. The festive season is one of the biggest opportunities for consumer brands to improve sales, acquire new customers and build market share.
Beyond tracking the growth of India's consumer brands, Entrackr is also looking to build a stronger founder community through The Spur – The D2C Mixer. The idea is to bring D2C founders together in an informal setting where they can step away from their everyday business routines, meet peers, exchange experiences and have meaningful conversations. As these brands continue to scale, a community where founders can connect, learn from each other's journeys and share challenges becomes equally important. The Spur is an effort to create that space, without panels, pitches or formal presentations. The focus remains on genuine conversations and long term connections.
The opportunity ahead is also significant. According to IBEF, India's D2C market is projected to reach $60 billion by 2030. A separate estimate by NeoMa Capital puts the total addressable market (TAM) for D2C brands at around $100 billion in FY26, including online and offline consumer discretionary spending. However, the currently obtainable market through brand websites and direct channels is estimated at $25 billion. This highlights the headroom for homegrown consumer brands to expand their presence and capture a larger share of India's growing consumption market.
D2C startups are an important part of India's startup ecosystem. They bring a certain charm to the ecosystem through new brands, products that reach consumers and challenges to established players across categories. The next few years could see many more homegrown brands emerge, scale and become household names. The real opportunity is not just in raising capital but in building businesses that can stand the test of time.

title: PhysicsWallah cites AI efficiencies for job cuts; offline biz faces profit pressure, earmarks $20 Mn for M&A
summary:
Edtech company PhysicsWallah is using artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiencies and reduce its workforce requirements, even as it looks to expand through inorganic route — acquisitions. The Noida-based company also continues to face profitability challenges in its offline business, despite the expansion of its Vidyapeeth centres.
During its Q2 FY27 earnings call, management confirmed that its total employee count, which stood at around 19,100, and faculty strength of approximately 7,100 declined sequentially in the quarter. The firm attributed the reduction partly to efficiencies from AI across content creation, quality checks, test paper preparation and evaluation.
Management said AI now writes around 90% of the company's code. The shift towards automation has also helped contain employee expenses, which declined 2.3% year-on-year in Q2 FY27, excluding ESOP costs. For the first half of FY27, employee expenses were down 2.4% compared to the same period last year.
However, PhysicsWallah continues to invest in technology which stood at Rs 104 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 70 crore in the corresponding period last year.
While AI-led efficiencies have helped improve operating leverage, PhysicsWallah's offline business remains a key area to watch. The segment reported a pre-Ind AS EBITDA loss of Rs 108 crore in H1 FY27, compared to Rs 120 crore in the year-ago period, as per figures discussed during the call.
The offline business reported 9% year-on-year revenue growth to Rs 541 crore in Q2 FY27, while H1 revenue rose 12% to Rs 1,031 crore. Management attributed the moderation in growth partly to lower NEET enrolments and delays in government exam notifications, which affected demand at some of its centres.

PhysicsWallah operates 370 offline centres, including 167 Vidyapeeth centres, compared to 117 in the previous year. Vidyapeeth contributed around 66% of the company's offline business collections in H1 FY27. Management said the standalone Vidyapeeth business is already profitable and expects the broader offline segment to move closer to breakeven. The company plans to add 25-30 offline centres annually over the next two to three years, while keeping a tighter check on upfront costs.

title: FamApp’s revenue touches Rs 25 Cr in FY26, profit nosedives 99%
summary:
FamPay Solutions Private Limited, the entity behind fintech app FamApp, reported a 20.5% increase in revenue from operations and crossed the Rs 25 crore milestone in FY26. However, higher employee and other operating expenses sharply reduced its profit by 99%.
The Bengaluru-based company has reported a 20.5% increase in operating revenue to Rs 25.02 crore in FY26 from Rs 20.75 crore in FY25, according to its standalone financial statements reviewed by Entrackr.
With Rs 5.01 crore in interest income and Rs 5.2 crore in gains from the sale of investments, its total income increased 13.1% to Rs 35.23 crore during the last fiscal year. It's important to note that the financials presented here are based on its standalone statements.

Expenses, meanwhile, grew 34.7% to Rs 35.18 crore, outpacing revenue growth. Employee benefit expenses increased 23.3% to Rs 16.16 crore, while other expenses rose 47.1% to Rs 18.45 crore. Its technical fees saw a jump of 82% to Rs 10.22 crore in FY26
Consequently, profit before tax fell to Rs 4.8 lakh in the fiscal year ending March 2026 from Rs 5.04 crore in the previous year.
The balance sheet showed cash and cash equivalents of Rs 61.83 crore as of March 2026, up from Rs 20.62 crore a year earlier. Current investments, however, declined to Rs 26.5 crore from Rs 54.6 crore. 
The financial performance comes amid changes in FamApp’s reset. In June 2025, Entrackr reported that Elevation Capital led a $15 million secondary round in the company, with a large part of the investment going towards purchasing shares held by co-founder Kush Taneja. Taneja subsequently exited the company.
FamApp’s financial performance points to a business at a critical stage of its evolution. The challenge now is to establish whether its revenue growth can support a more efficient operating model as it expands. The sharp erosion in profitability raises questions about the cost of scaling and the sustainability of its current economics. 
While its cash reserves provide room to invest in the business, the focus will need to shift towards improving operating leverage and building a more predictable earnings profile. It is important to note that these numbers reflect FamPay Solutions’ standalone performance and not the consolidated one. Its ability to balance growth with cost discipline will determine whether it can build a durable fintech business.

title: DriveU’s net profit doubles in FY26; NTV grows to Rs 131 Cr
summary:
India’s mobility market is largely dominated by ride-hailing platforms such as Uber, Ola and Rapido, which connect consumers with taxis and two-wheeler services. However, a parallel market for on-demand drivers is emerging, particularly among car owners who seek a convenient alternative to driving themselves. Concerns around drunk driving and road safety have further fuelled demand for such services, creating opportunities for platforms such as DriveU, which allow customers to hire verified drivers to drive their own vehicles.
DriveU continued to scale its business while maintaining profitability for the third consecutive financial year. During the fiscal year ended March 2026, the company more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore, while its net revenue grew 14% year-on-year.
The Bengaluru-based company’s net revenue increased to Rs 32.9 crore in FY26 from Rs 28.9 crore in FY25, according to its audited financial statements.

Founded in 2015 by father-son duo Ashok Shastry and Rahm Shastry, DriveU offers trained, verified drivers on demand for customers’ own cars. It also operates DriveU Reserve, a premium cab service, and DriveU Coach, an at-home driving lessons platform. The company operates in 13 cities and has completed over 10.5 million trips with more than 100,000 registered driver-partners.
The company’s net transaction value (NTV) increased 17% to Rs 131 crore in FY26 from Rs 112 crore in the previous fiscal year. Its gross revenue stood at Rs 131 crore during the year.
On the expense side, DriveU paid around Rs 97.21 crore to driver-partners during FY26. Employee benefit expenses remained stable at Rs 13.7 crore.
Direct expenses, including partner incentives, technology costs and trip insurance, stood at Rs 8.35 crore. Meanwhile, business promotion and marketing expenses declined 5% year-on-year to Rs 4.84 crore. Overall, the company’s expenses grew 10% to Rs 30.5 crore during FY26.
On the profitability front, DriveU more than doubled its net profit to Rs 3.6 crore in FY26 from Rs 1.73 crore in FY25, maintaining profitability for the third consecutive year. Its EBITDA grew 58% year-on-year to Rs 2.74 crore, while the EBITDA margin on net revenue improved to 8.3% from 6% in the previous fiscal year.

As of March 2026, it had cash and bank balances of Rs 12 crore and total current assets of Rs 20 crore.
DriveU has raised a total of Rs 54 crore since its inception, with its last funding round taking place in 2024. The company has not raised any fresh capital since then.
Beyond its core driver-on-demand business, the company launched two new verticals in April 2026: DriveU Reserve, a chauffeur-driven premium cab service, and DriveU Coach, which provides driving lessons at customers’ homes.
The company expects its gross revenue to reach Rs 170 crore in FY27, representing a growth of around 30% over FY26. It plans to expand both Reserve and Coach into more cities, while funding investments in these businesses through operating cash flows.

title: Funding and acquisitions in Indian startups this week [Nov 02- Nov 07]
summary:
This week, 28 Indian startups raised $258.1 million across three growth-stage deals and 17 early-stage deals, including two undisclosed rounds. The week also saw nine key appointments and one departure, two fund launches, an ESOP buyback and an acquisition.

In contrast, 28 startups had collectively secured about $115 million in the previous week.
[Growth-stage deals]
Growth-stage startups raised $190.5 million across three deals this week. Jewellery brand GIVA led the pack with a $100 million funding round led by Multiples Alternate Asset Management. Bengaluru-based consumer AI and entertainment company EloElo Group followed with an $80 million Series C round led by Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal.
Pune-based robotics startup Peppermint Robotics raised Rs 100 crore (around $10.5 million) in a Pre-Series B round led by pi Ventures and Crane Venture Partners.
[Early-stage deals]
Early-stage startups raised $67.6 million across 17 deals this week. Pune-based health-tech startup Clinics On Cloud led with a $12.5 million Series A round from Dubai-based investors through Model42, powered by Enlightened Minds Investments. Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM followed with a $10.3 million Series A round led by Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures.
AI-powered clean energy platform Two Point O Capital (TW\.O) raised $10 million in a round led by Transition Venture Capital, while wealthtech platform PowerUp Money secured $10 million led by Flourish Ventures, with participation from existing investors including Peak XV Partners, Accel and Blume Ventures.
Other startups that raised funding this week included spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space, defence technology company Axial Aero, AI-powered autonomous delivery robot developer Ottonomy, biotechnology companyVenomics AI , QSR startup The Croffle Guys and others. 
[City and segment-wise deals]
Bengaluru led startup funding activity with 6 deals during the week, followed by Delhi-NCR and Mumbai with five deals each. Pune, Hyderabad, and Gandhinagar also recorded funding this week.

E-commerce and AI startups led sector-wise funding activity with three deals each, followed by healthtech, manufacturing, fintech, foodtech and gaming, with two deals each. Robotics, spacetech and deeptech startups also secured funding during the week.
[Series-wise deals]
Seed rounds led funding activity with eight deals, followed by Series A and pre-seed rounds with four and three deals, respectively. Series C, pre-Series B, pre-Series A and angel rounds also saw activity during the week.

[Week-on-week funding trend]
On a weekly basis, startup funding more than doubled to $258.1 million from $115 million raised in the previous week.
The average weekly funding over the past eight weeks stood at around $198 million across 23 deals.
[Key Hirings]
Logistics company Porter has appointed Gaurav Jain as its chief financial officer (CFO), while Shubham Gupta and Mohit Rathi have been elevated to chief technology officer (CTO) and chief marketing officer (CMO), respectively.
Enterprise AI and analytics firm MathCo appointed Vijay Raj to its advisory board. Avendus named Sumit Agarwal as managing director and head of equity corporate finance, while Fulcrum Digital appointed Latha Nathan as senior vice president of India delivery operations. UiPath also named Yashdeep Vaishnav as its India country manager. Avendus appointed Sumit Agarwal as Managing Director and Head of Equity Corporate Finance.

Cashfree, an AI-native payments platform, has launched Checkout for Agents, becoming the first Indian payments company to integrate the WebMCP standard into its checkout. The feature enables AI agents to complete transactions on behalf of consumers and is available across Cashfree’s hosted checkout, payment forms and payment links without requiring merchants to change their existing integrations. WebMCP allows AI agents to interact with websites through a defined set of actions instead of decoding page layouts and underlying code, potentially reducing token consumption during checkout by over 40%.

title: Sugar Cosmetics cuts losses by 41% in FY26, revenue dips 11%
summary:
After a difficult period for the beauty and personal care brand, Sugar Cosmetics showed some improvement in its financial performance in FY26, with a sharp reduction in expenses helping it narrow losses. However, the company continued to face pressure on revenue, which declined for the fiscal year ending March 2026.
Sugar Brands, the parent entity of Sugar Cosmetics, reported revenue from operations of Rs 361 crore in FY26, down 10.7% from Rs 404.4 crore in FY25, according to its consolidated financial statements reviewed by Entrackr. Including other income of Rs 2.85 crore, its total income stood at Rs 364 crore, compared with Rs 411.7 crore in the previous fiscal.


The decline in revenue came amid a challenging period for the company, which has faced pressure in a competitive beauty market. Its expenses, however, fell at a faster pace than revenue. Total expenses declined 18.9% to Rs 443 crore in FY26 from Rs 546.5 crore in FY25.
Advertising and sales promotion remained the largest expense item, although the company cut this outlay by 28.9% to Rs 119.4 crore from Rs 168 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses fell 21.2% to Rs 58.7 crore, while outsourced support services costs declined to Rs 61.4 crore from Rs 76 crore. Finance costs also decreased 34.8% to Rs 5.6 crore.
The lower cost base helped Sugar Brands narrow its net loss by 41% to Rs 79.3 crore in FY26 from Rs 134.3 crore in the previous year.

On a unit level, the company spent Rs 1.23 for every rupee of operating revenue in FY26, compared with Rs 1.35 in FY25. Its EBITDA margin improved to -20.02% in FY26 from -30.56% in the previous fiscal, while ROCE stood at -129.51%.



The company ended FY26 with cash and bank balances of Rs 10.30 crore, compared with Rs 23 crore a year earlier.

The financial performance comes at a crucial point for Sugar. The company recently raised fresh capital at a valuation that was reportedly around 80% below its peak, representing the reset in investor expectations after a difficult period. The funding could provide some room to reassess its business, strengthen distribution and focus on improving the economics of its core operations.
Competition remains another challenge for Sugar. Rival Renee Cosmetics recorded 37% growth in operating revenue to Rs 440 crore in FY26 and also cut its losses by 45%, pointing out the pace at which newer brands are scaling in the beauty and personal care market. The growth puts further pressure on Sugar to defend its market position and regain momentum.
However, Sugar’s FY26 numbers offer some grounds for optimism. The firm reduced its cost base and narrowed losses even as revenue dipped. While Renee’s performance highlights the competitive pressure, Sugar still has an opportunity to bring its business back on track by sharpening its product portfolio, strengthening distribution and improving unit economics. 
Many durable consumer businesses have had to navigate difficult phases before finding a sustainable growth model. For Sugar, the next test will be whether it can translate the financial discipline of FY26 into renewed revenue growth without returning to its earlier cost structure.

title: MakeMyTrip acquires majority stake in Quick Ride to enter shared mobility segment
summary:
Travel technology platform MakeMyTrip has acquired a majority stake in Bengaluru-based shared mobility startup Quick Ride, marking its entry into the ride pooling segment. The acquisition will expand MakeMyTrip’s ground transportation portfolio and strengthen its presence in daily urban commutes.
Entrackr exclusively reported on October 19 that MakeMyTrip was in talks to acquire Quick Ride through its subsidiary redBus. However, the financial details of the transaction have not been disclosed.









Founded in 2015 by KNM Rao, Quick Ride is an asset-light mobility platform that connects people travelling along similar routes for car and bike pooling. It enables users to share rides for everyday commutes and offers services to corporate employees through partnerships with companies, IT parks and business campuses. The platform aims to make commuting more affordable while reducing the number of vehicles on roads.
According to MakeMyTrip, Quick Ride’s ride pooling business and brand have undergone an internal restructuring and are now housed under a new entity, Co Ride Mobility Private Limited. MakeMyTrip has acquired the brand and its ride pooling business through a majority stake in this entity. Quick Ride’s promoters will continue to lead the business, while its erstwhile EV taxi business will remain with the predecessor entity, iDisha Info Labs Private Limited.
Commenting on the development, Rajesh Magow, Co-founder and Group CEO of MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will help the company establish a presence in high-frequency daily commutes within cities, alongside intercity travel. He added that Quick Ride will be housed under MakeMyTrip’s ground transport business, which will leverage its experience in building redBus in India and overseas markets to scale the platform.
Prakash Sangam, CEO of redBus and Head of Ground Transport at MakeMyTrip, said the acquisition will expand the company’s offerings across different travel needs. The platform sees an opportunity to serve the same customers across their daily office commutes and intercity journeys.
Quick Ride has raised funding from investors including Sequoia Capital India (now Peak XV Partners), Naspers (now part of Prosus) and Venture Highway. In 2019, the company raised Rs 100.78 crore ($14.4 million) in a Series B round from its existing investors.
The acquisition is part of MakeMyTrip’s strategy to expand its presence across travel segments through acquisitions and strategic investments. In recent years, the company has acquired Savaari in the car rental segment, Happay in corporate travel and expense management, and Flamingo Transworld in regional group holiday packages. It has also made a strategic minority investment in visa processing platform Atlys.
The latest acquisition adds ride pooling to its ground transportation portfolio, which already includes redBus and Savaari. The company said the addition of Quick Ride will help it offer customers a wider range of travel options, from daily commutes to intercity journeys.

title: Mamaearth parent Honasa profit jumps 87% to Rs 73 Cr in Q2 FY27, revenue grows 36%
summary:
Honasa Consumer, the parent company of Mamaearth, announced its financial results for the second quarter of the fiscal year ending March 2027. The company reported a 36% year-on-year growth in its revenue during the quarter, while its net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore.
The Gurugram-based company's revenue from operations increased to Rs 731 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 538 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, according to its financial statements accessed from the National Stock Exchange of India (NSE).

The firm also recorded Rs 22 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 753 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 558 crore in Q2 FY26.
On the expense front, the cost of materials consumed remained the largest expense component, increasing 38.4% to Rs 220 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 159 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Employee benefit expenses also increased 21.7% to Rs 73 crore. Depreciation expenses, however, marginaly declined  to Rs 11 crore from Rs 11.75 crore.
Other expenses rose 26.9% to Rs 348 crore which pushed its total expenses by 29.1% to Rs 652 crore during the last quarter.
At the bottom line, Honasa Consumer’s net profit surged 86.7% to Rs 73.25 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39.23 crore in Q2 FY26.
For the first half of FY27, Honasa Consumer's revenue from operations grew 31.2% to Rs 1,487 crore from Rs 1,133 crore in H1 FY26.
Meanwhile, its net profit jumped 2.03X to Rs 164 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 80.5 crore in the corresponding period last year. The firm’s total income stood at Rs 1,531 crore in H1 FY27, compared with Rs 1,177 crore in H1 FY26.
The company's shares were trading at Rs 487 as of 1:35 PM, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 15,703 crore.

title: Angel One overtakes Zerodha to become second-largest broker; Groww adds over 3 lakh clients in October
summary:
Angel One overtook Zerodha to become India’s second-largest stock broker in October 2026, adding nearly 2.43 lakh active clients during the month. Meanwhile, Groww maintained its leadership position with over 1.37 crore active clients, while discount broking platform Sahi recorded the fastest monthly growth among the top 20 brokers.
According to data from the National Stock Exchange (NSE), the total active client base increased 1.33% month-on-month to 4.67 crore in October from 4.61 crore in September, an addition of nearly 6.15 lakh clients.
Groww retained its dominant position with 1.37 crore active clients in October, adding the highest number of clients at 3.04 lakh during the month. Its market share stood at 29.43%, the highest among stock brokers in India.
Angel One moved to the second position with 69.98 lakh active clients, an addition of 2.43 lakh clients during the month. Its market share increased to 14.97%.
Zerodha slipped to the third position with 67.59 lakh active clients, down 32,435 from 67.91 lakh in September. Its market share stood at 14.46%.

ICICI Securities retained the fourth position with 21.64 lakh active clients, adding 3,722 clients during the month. Upstox held the fifth spot with 18.43 lakh active clients, despite a decline of 11,348 clients. Their respective market shares stood at 4.63% and 3.94%.
Among other major brokers, Kotak Securities added 12,895 clients to reach 14.05 lakh, while HDFC Securities' active client base increased to 13.60 lakh from 13.54 lakh in September.
Dhan added 25,739 active clients during October to reach 11.47 lakh, with its market share standing at 2.45%. SBI Securities saw its client base decline by 17,188 to 10.04 lakh, taking its market share to 2.15%. Motilal Oswal added 7,283 clients to reach 9.16 lakh, with a market share of 1.96%.
Paytm Money recorded the steepest decline among the top 20 brokers, with a loss of 32,501 active clients, down 4.26% month-on-month to 7.30 lakh. In contrast, INDmoney added 1,849 clients to reach 7.21 lakh.
Sahi emerged as the fastest-growing broker among the top 20 in October, following an 11% increase in its active client base in September. The platform added 34,372 clients during the month, taking its total to 3.15 lakh. Its market share stood at 0.67%.
PhonePe's Share.Market added 7,041 active clients to reach 2.14 lakh in October. IIFL Securities also added 5,095 clients, taking its active client base to 3.46 lakh.

title: Sleepy Owl’s revenue surges 86% to Rs 82 Cr in FY26; nears breakeven
summary:
Coffee has become a part of everyday conversations, with more Indians exploring different varieties and flavours. While many people prefer Brazilian or Vietnamese coffee, not everyone knows that India is the world's fifth-largest coffee exporter among coffee-producing nations, accounting for around 5% of global exports.
This growing interest has also given rise to several homegrown coffee brands trying to find their place in the market. One of them is Sleepy Owl, which has grown nearly 4X in the past three years, increasing its revenue from Rs 21.5 crore in FY23 to Rs 82 crore in FY26.


Sleepy Owl’s revenue from operations grew 86.4% year-on-year to Rs 82 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 44 crore in FY25, according to its annual financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC).
Sleepy Owl is a homegrown coffee brand focused on the at-home coffee consumption market. Its product range includes cold brew, instant coffee, hot brew bags, ground coffee, and ready-to-drink coffee.
The sale of coffees are the primary source of revenue for Sleep Owl which includes coffee seches, can, bottles, coffee packets and boxes.
On the cost side, coffee procurement accounted for around 22% of its overall expenses. This cost grew 84.3% to Rs 43.5 crore in FY26. Employee benefit expenses also increased to Rs 9 crore during the fiscal year.
The company spent Rs 20 crore on advertising in FY26. Other expenses, including shipping, legal, technology and other operating costs, increased to Rs 85 crore from Rs 47 crore in FY25.


Sleepy Owl managed to reduce its net losses by 17% to Rs 1.76 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.12 crore in the previous fiscal year. The company is nearing breakeven, with its ROCE and EBITDA margin standing at -6% and -1.8%, respectively. On a unit level, it spent Rs 1.04 to earn every rupee of revenue in FY26.
Building a business around coffee for home consumption has not been easy, and several startups have tried to crack this market. In that sense, Sleepy Owl reaching Rs 82 crore in revenue and bringing its losses close to breakeven is a good sign for the company. The competition, however, is getting stronger. Blue Tokai and Third Wave Coffee are also growing their businesses, with the former recently raising $25 million and reportedly looking to extend its Series D round. Blue Tokai and Third Wave Coffee reported revenues of Rs 325 crore and Rs 285 crore, respectively. Established players such as Tata Starbucks and Cafe Coffee Day are much larger, with revenues of Rs 1,367 crore and Rs 1,094 crore, respectively. For Sleepy Owl, the real test will be to maintain this growth and turn the business profitable as competition in the coffee market heats up.

title: Spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space raises $6 Mn in seed round
summary:
Hyderabad-based spacetech startup Cosmoserve Space has raised $6 million in a seed funding round from Japan-based Rebright Partners, Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures and existing investors AUM Ventures and Shakti VC. The latest round takes its total funding to over $9 million.
In September last year, the startup raised $3.17 million in an oversubscribed pre-seed round led by Alan Rutledge, with participation from AUM Ventures and Shakti VC.
The fresh capital will support the development of Base 1, technology demonstrations and two upcoming missions, Cosmoserve said in a press release.
The startup has also inaugurated Base 1, a private facility dedicated to space debris removal and satellite servicing. The facility is designed to support the development of technologies for in-orbit repairs, refuelling and the recovery of defunct satellites.
According to the company, Base 1 is the world’s sixth facility equipped with space vision effects and microgravity simulation capabilities. It brings together infrastructure for designing, building, testing and operating technologies required for satellite servicing and space debris recovery.
Cosmoserve currently sources nearly 60% of its mission components locally. It aims to increase domestic manufacturing by developing critical technologies in-house and reducing dependence on imported optics, avionics and space-grade electronics.
In July 2026, Cosmoserve flew its first payload, Mission Embrace, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. The flight hardware was developed in under four months, six months ahead of schedule. However, the robotic capture petals did not deploy as planned, providing the company with data for further development.
Founded last year by Chiranjeevi Phanindra, Cosmoserve is developing a proprietary Dual Spacecraft Architecture to make orbital servicing more cost-efficient. The approach uses two spacecraft to service multiple satellites, instead of the conventional one-to-one recovery model.
The company estimates that its approach could bring satellite servicing costs down from around $10 million to below $1 million per satellite.
Cosmoserve plans to test its robotic capture systems through microgravity flights, reflight Mission Embrace and conduct a full-scale space debris capture demonstration in 2027.
The startup is among a growing number of Indian spacetech companies working on technologies spanning launch vehicles, satellite manufacturing, space data and orbital infrastructure. Hyderabad has also emerged as a spacetech hub, supported by its aerospace and defence ecosystem, engineering talent and research infrastructure.

title: Moneyview's Q2 FY27 profit jumps 5.15X to Rs 201 Cr
summary:
Digital lending platform Moneyview reported a 41% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in Q2 FY27, while its net profit jumped 5.15 times during the period.
Moneyview’s revenue from operations rose to Rs 1,120 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 794 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, according to its consolidated financial statements filed with the National Stock Exchange (NSE).
The Bengaluru-based company also reported Rs 26 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 1,146 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 804.6 crore in Q2 FY26.
Founded in 2014 by Puneet Agarwal and Sanjay Aggarwal, Moneyview provides digital lending products such as instant personal loans, credit cards, Buy Now Pay Later (BNPL) and financial management solutions through partner lenders. Its lending partners include Aditya Birla Capital, Northern Arc, Vivriti Capital and Oxyzo.
Impairment of financial instruments increased 18.7% to Rs 286 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 241 crore in Q2 FY26. Employee benefits expenses rose 41.3% to Rs 97.5 crore from Rs 69 crore during the same period.
Finance costs increased 25.6% to Rs 194 crore from Rs 154.5 crore, while other expenses grew 24.6% to Rs 298.5 crore from Rs 239.5 crore. Overall, Moneyview's total expenses increased 24.5% to Rs 876.5 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 704 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year.
At the bottom line, the company's net profit surged 5.15 times to Rs 201 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 39 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal year, marking a 415.4% year-on-year increase.
On a half-yearly basis, Moneyview's revenue from operations grew 45.3% to Rs 2,161 crore in H1 FY27 from Rs 1,487 crore in H1 FY26. Its net profit increased 253.8% to Rs 375 crore from Rs 106 crore during the same period.
At the close of Thursday’s trading session, the company's shares settled at Rs 58.25, giving it a market capitalisation of approximately Rs 9,701 crore.

title: Daksham Growth Ventures raises Rs 125 Cr in first close of maiden consumer fund
summary:
Daksham Growth Ventures (DGV), the growth investment platform of multi-family office and private wealth management group Daksham Capital, has raised Rs 125 crore in the first close of its maiden consumer-focused fund, DGV Fund I.
Registered as a Category II Alternative Investment Fund (AIF) with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the fund has a target corpus of Rs 150 crore, along with a greenshoe option of another Rs 150 crore, taking its potential fund size to Rs 300 crore.
The first close was anchored by family offices, high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), ultra-high-net-worth individuals (UHNIs) and entrepreneurs. The fund achieved the first close shortly after receiving SEBI registration in October 2026.
Led by Shivam Diwan, Co-Founder and Managing Partner of Daksham Growth Ventures, the fund will primarily invest in pre-Series A and Series A companies across India’s consumer ecosystem.
DGV Fund I plans to invest Rs 5 crore to Rs 20 crore in businesses that have established product-market fit and sound unit economics. It will focus on companies with annual recurring revenue (ARR) of Rs 25-75 crore and the potential to scale to Rs 300-500 crore in revenue.
The fund’s investment strategy spans four segments: direct-to-consumer (D2C) brands, consumer enablers, B2B2C and supply chain businesses, and consumer-focused artificial intelligence (AI) companies.
Beyond capital, DGV plans to support its portfolio companies through governance, financial reporting, brand positioning, leadership development and distribution expansion. The fund will also provide board participation, strategic guidance and access to industry networks to help businesses strengthen their organisational capabilities.
Daksham Capital operates across family office advisory, investment solutions, global investing, legacy and succession planning, investment banking advisory and structured lending solutions. The group said its team has advised more than 600 client families and previously managed over $1 billion in assets.
Daksham Growth Ventures is the group’s dedicated growth investment platform, focusing on consumer and consumer-allied businesses with established business models and the potential to scale sustainably.

title: Bio-tech startup Venomics AI raises $2.7 Mn in pre-seed round
summary:
Venomics AI, a biotechnology company spun out of the Indian Institute of Science (IISc), has raised $2.7 million in its first institutional funding round. The pre-seed round was co-led by Speciale Invest and South Park Commons, with participation from Operators Studio.
The proceeds will be used to expand the company’s operations, grow its molecular dataset and strengthen its AI and laboratory screening capabilities, Venomics AI said in a press release.
Co-founded in May 2026 by Sunagar and Vinay Prabhu, Venomics AI combines venom biology, molecular sequencing, AI and experimental screening to discover and develop venom-derived therapeutic leads.
The Bengaluru-based startup is building the Venom Atlas, a platform that connects venom-derived molecular data with laboratory validation and drug discovery. It uses AI to prioritise molecular candidates and tests these predictions through functional screening in the laboratory. The experimental results are then fed back into subsequent predictions and molecular design.
The company aims to use India’s venom biodiversity and its scientific and computational expertise to develop a drug discovery platform for global therapeutic development.
Venomics AI has established the initial architecture of its platform, joined the NVIDIA Inception programme and been selected among the top five finalists for the 2026 Indo-Boston Biotech Bridge Award.

title: Tonbo Imaging turns profitable in Q2 FY27 with Rs 23.5 Cr; shares hit 20% upper circuit
summary:
Defence technology company Tonbo Imaging reported over 20X year-on-year growth in revenue from operations in its first quarterly results (Q2 FY27) after listing on the stock exchanges. The company also turned profitable during the quarter.
Tonbo Imaging’s revenue from operations increased to Rs 183.3 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 8.9 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its consolidated financial statement sourced from NSE.

Founded by Ankit Kumar, Arvind Kondangi Lakshmikumar and Cecilia D'Souza, Tonbo Imaging develops advanced imaging and surveillance technologies for defence and security applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, targeting solutions, missile seekers and fire control systems.
Tonbo Imaging's total income stood at Rs 185.2 crore during the quarter, including Rs 1.9 crore from non-operating income.
As the company scaled up its operations, its expenses also increased in line with scale. Cost of materials consumed was the largest expense component, accounting for over 78% of total expenses at Rs 120.9 crore during the quarter.
Employee benefits expenses remained largely flat at around Rs 12 crore in Q2 FY27, while depreciation and amortisation expenses and finance costs stood at Rs 9.8 crore and Rs 4.8 crore, respectively.
Overall, Tonbo Imaging's total expenses surged over 7 times year-on-year to Rs 153.7 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 21.6 crore in the corresponding quarter last fiscal.
A 20.6X growth in operating revenue helped Tonbo Imaging turn profitable during the quarter, with a net profit of Rs 23.5 crore against a net loss of Rs 9.6 crore in Q2 FY26.
On a sequential basis, Tonbo Imaging's revenue from operations increased over 5 times from Rs 36 crore in the previous quarter. The company had reported a net loss of Rs 17.7 crore in Q2 FY26.
Following the strong quarterly performance, Tonbo Imaging's share price surged 20% and hit the upper circuit at Rs 1,530.3 apiece at 1:10 PM today, taking its market capitalisation to Rs 8,766 crore.

title: Decathlon India’s total income crosses Rs 4,500 Cr in FY26;  EBITDA stands at Rs 424 Cr
summary:
As interest in sports beyond cricket continues to grow in India, people are increasingly taking up activities such as badminton, hockey, boxing, swimming, trekking and skating. This has also created opportunities for brands catering to a wider range of sporting needs. One such brand is Decathlon, which offers products across multiple sports categories under one roof. Let's decode how the sporting goods retailer performed financially in FY26.
French sporting goods retailer Decathlon's Indian arm reported an 8.35% year-on-year growth in revenue from operations to Rs 4,478 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,133 crore in FY25.
Started in India in 2009, Decathlon has grown into one of the country's largest sporting goods retailers. The company currently operates 132 stores across India and is targeting an expansion to 200 stores by 2030.

The sale of sporting goods and apparel remains its primary source of revenue. Its product portfolio includes clothing, footwear, trekking gear, fitness equipment and accessories across various sports categories. The company also added Rs 39 crore in other income, taking its total income to Rs 4,517 crore in FY26.
On the cost side, the procurement of materials and sporting goods remained the largest expense, accounting for nearly 64% of the overall expenditure. This cost increased 7.4% to Rs 2,840 crore in FY26 from Rs 2,644 crore in FY25. Employee benefit expenses also rose 12% to Rs 407 crore during the fiscal year.
Other expenses, including rent, franchisee fees, freight, credit card commissions and IT support charges, pushed the company's total expenditure up 4% to Rs 4,435 crore in FY26, compared to Rs 4,264 crore in FY25.
Despite the increase in costs, Decathlon India managed to turn profitable during the fiscal year. The company posted a net profit of Rs 63 crore in FY26, against a loss of Rs 65 crore in FY25. It also reported an EBITDA of Rs 424 crore during the year.


On a unit level, Decathlon spent Rs 0.99 to earn every rupee of operating revenue in FY26. Its return on capital employed (ROCE) and EBITDA margin stood at 7.6% and 9%, respectively. The company had total current assets of Rs 1,686 crore at the end of the fiscal year.
Decathlon has been hovering around the Rs 4,000 crore revenue mark for the past few years. To move beyond this, the company will have to expand its reach to more cities and states, something it is already working on. Its plans to expand in Europe and export more products manufactured in India could also open up new growth opportunities. The India-EU FTA may further help, depending on how the agreement shapes up. At the same time, adding more categories and bringing new products to Indian consumers will remain important. It will be interesting to see how Decathlon takes this forward and how soon it can cross the Rs 5,000 crore revenue mark.

title: Exclusive: Scripbox to convert into public company ahead of IPO plans
summary:
Bengaluru-based wealthtech startup Scripbox is set to convert into a public company after passing a resolution approving the move, a step that signals its preparation for a potential public listing.
According to regulatory filings accessed by Entrackr, Scripbox’s board has passed a resolution to approve its conversion into a public limited company by changing its legal name from “Scripbox Wealth Managers Private Limited” to “Scripbox Wealth Managers Limited”.
As per the filing, the proposed initial public offering (IPO) will comprise a fresh issue of equity shares and an offer for sale (OFS) by certain existing shareholders of the company.
Founded in 2012 by Atul Shinghal and Sanjiv Singhal, Scripbox operates a digital wealth management platform that offers investment products across mutual funds, fixed deposits, US stocks, ETFs and the National Pension System (NPS), along with financial planning and advisory services.
The development comes nearly six months after Entrackr exclusively reported that Scripbox was planning to raise up to Rs 170 crore through a mix of debt and equity.
As part of the proposed fundraise, Scripbox's board had approved raising up to Rs 60 crore from a select group of investors through equity shares, preference shares and convertible instruments. It had also secured approval to raise up to Rs 110 crore through debt from banks, NBFCs and other financial institutions. 
In June this year, the company acquired the mutual fund distribution business of Delhi-NCR-based Bluechip Capital, a wealth management firm founded and led by Ravi Kohli for over 33 years. The transaction also saw Bluechip Capital's clients and employees transition to Scripbox.
Scripbox has raised over $70 million through a mix of equity and debt from investors including Accel, LetsVenture and DMI.
On the financial front, Scripbox turned profitable in FY25 with a net profit of Rs 12.7 crore, while its operating revenue grew 27% year-on-year to Rs 107.2 crore. The company is yet to disclose its FY26 financial results.

title: Specialty chemicals startup altM raises $10.3 Mn led by Rainmatter, Mela Ventures
summary:
Bengaluru-based specialty chemicals startup altM has raised $10.3 million in a Series A funding round led by new investors Rainmatter by Zerodha and Mela Ventures. The round also saw participation from existing investors Omnivore, Theia Ventures, Aureolis Ventures and Spectrum Impact, along with VC Grid and strategic angel investors.
The company will use the fresh capital to expand its manufacturing capabilities, research and development, customer qualification programmes, and engineering and commercial teams as it moves from pilot-scale production to commercial manufacturing.
Founded in 2022 by former Tesla manufacturing leaders Apoorv Garg and Yugal Raj Jain, altM is developing a specialty chemicals platform that converts agricultural residue into high-performance industrial chemicals. Bioprocessing scientist Dr Harshad Velankar later joined the company as its chief scientific officer.
The company's platform converts lignocellulosic biomass, including sugarcane bagasse and rice straw, into materials for beauty and personal care, textiles, industrial chemicals, construction, packaging and consumer goods.
It uses cellulose, hemicellulose and lignin to produce multiple products from a single feedstock. The process enables agricultural residue to serve as a source of industrial carbon and reduces dependence on fossil-derived raw materials.
Since raising $3.5 million in a seed round in 2023, altM has built an integrated R&D and pilot manufacturing facility in Bengaluru. The facility brings laboratory research, demonstration manufacturing and pilot production under one roof.
The company has expanded its laboratory footprint nearly fivefold, commissioned its demonstration manufacturing facility and advanced six molecules to demonstration scale. Three of these have been selected for pilot plant production.
Its first products moving towards commercialisation include a lignin-derived SPF booster for suncare applications, a cellulose-based rheology modifier and bio-derived ferulic acid for cosmetics and personal care formulations.
altM competes with Scimplifi, Covvalent, Atomgrid and Tulon Materials, which have also raised fresh funding this year.
The latest funding will help altM scale its manufacturing operations and expand customer deployments as it seeks to build a platform for producing industrial chemicals from agricultural residue.
